chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Muhammad al-Mad'ini, from A'idh ibn Habib, the seller of al-Harawi, from Isa ibn Zayd, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The boy's teeth are cut (circumcised) at seven years, and he is commanded to pray at seven years, and they separate him from them in the sleeping places at ten, and he has a seminal emission at fourteen, and his height ends at twenty-two years, and the end of his intellect is at twenty-eight years, except for experiences.

key_terms.مُنْتَهَى عَقْلِهِ: The end/peak of his intellect (full mental maturity)
key_terms.يَثَّغِرُ: Circumcises (specifically for males, referring to cutting the foreskin)
key_terms.يَحْتَلِمُ: He experiences seminal emission (sign of puberty)
key_terms.يُؤْمَرُ بِالصَّلَاةِ: Is commanded to perform prayer (indicating the start of obligatory worship)
key_terms.يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَهُمْ فِي الْمَضَاجِعِ: They are separated in their sleeping places (referring to modesty and privacy from parents)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific ages for a boy's physical and legal milestones in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the foundational timeline for a boy’s transition from childhood to legal adulthood (bulugh) within Shia fiqh, linking physical signs like seminal emission to the onset of religious obligations. It highlights the gradual imposition of duties, starting with circumcision and prayer at age seven, while distinguishing between physical maturity and the fullness of intellect at twenty-eight, acknowledging empirical variation. This framework is crucial for determining when a male minor becomes fully accountable for his deeds in Islamic law.
